text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended on Thursday.

LONDON - UK shares ended lower for the first time this week, unsettled by declines on Wall Street and renewed talk of an imminent UK interest rate rise. The FTSE 100 closed at 4,907.5, down 19.8 points, or 0.40 percent.

FRANKFURT - The share market ended more than one percent lower, pressured by declines on Wall Street and profit taking. The DAX-30 index closed at 4,438.93, up 17.21 points, or 0.39 percent. In later screen-based trade the IBIS DAX index ended at 4,405.52, down 53.14 points, or 1.19 percent.

PARIS - Shares firmed to a fresh record close but came off the day's high after being dented by the U.S. Chicago Purchasing Managers Index, which stoked inflationary fears, traders said. The CAC-40 index closed at 3,075.67, up 6.37 points, or 0.21 percent.
ZURICH - Shares ended lower as investors took profits ahead of a three-day weekend in Switzerland. The Swiss market index closed at 5,898.2, down 31.3 points, or 0.53 percent.

TOKYO - Stocks ended higher as buying of blue chips accelerated in late afternoon, erasing losses created by racketeer scandal worries and a limping construction sector, brokers said. The 225-share Nikkei average closed at 20,331.43, up 118.61 points, or 0.59 percent.

HONG KONG - The Hang Seng Index closed at an all-time high as investors poured into the property sector boosting turnover to its highest level ever. The Hang Seng index closed at 16,365.71, up 382.53 points, or 2.39 percent.

SYDNEY - A lacklustre share market limped to a flat finish with a bullish streak on Wall Street ignored in favour of a wary eye on the upcoming local profit season. The All Ordinaries index closed at 2,735.1, up 0.1 points, or 0.00 percent.

JOHANNESBURG - Industrial shares finished stronger, propelled by positive sentiment from Wall Street and rallies on other world markets, dealers said. The All-share index closed at 7,484.5, up 10.8 points, or 0.14 percent. The All Gold index closed at 981.4, down 1.2 points, or 0.14 percent, while the Industrial index closed at 9,150.5, up 28.1 points, or 0.31 percent.
